issue.title: sase repo open reuses an external destination that is only a directory inside the host checkout (_is_valid_git_repo has no ceiling)
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-jf.1.2 (note #1) while implementing the SASE checkout-identity guard (sase commit a14bffcdbf, "fix(workspaces): guard Git mutations and pushes by checkout identity"). Triaged and independently reproduced by the bob-cli-jf.1 lander.

## What is wrong

`sase repo open <external ref>` decides whether to reuse its destination with `src/sase/main/repo_open_external.py::_is_valid_git_repo`. On sase origin/master (a14bffcdbf) that check runs `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` in the destination with no `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` and no root comparison. External destinations live under `<host>/sase/repos/external/...`, inside the host checkout. If the destination exists without its own `.git` (an empty or half-created directory, or a failed clone remnant), Git walks up to the host repo and the check returns true. `repo open` then reuses the path (line ~322) and prints it, so agents read, edit, and commit in what is really the host repository. That is the same root-cause class as the bob-cli-jf incident. The new push guard (`require_push_identity` → `require_worktree_root`) now refuses pushes from such a path, but local edits and commits still land in the host checkout.

## Reproduction (lander, 2026-11-10)

```
git init -q host && mkdir -p host/sase/repos/external/gh/example/child
cd host/sase/repos/external/gh/example/child
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree      # true  (what _is_valid_git_repo checks)
git rev-parse --show-toplevel            # <...>/host  (the enclosing host)
GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=$(dirname $PWD) git rev-parse --show-toplevel   # fatal: not a git repository
```

## Fix

Replace `_is_valid_git_repo` (all three call sites: reuse at ~322 and the temp/dest checks in `_atomic_external_clone` at ~424/~429) with the shared bounded probe `sase._git_worktree.is_worktree_root`, which a14bffcdbf added for linked and sidecar materialization. Optionally, match `ensure_git_clone_at` by removing an empty non-worktree destination and cloning fresh. Keep the existing "exists but is not a valid repository" error for nonempty non-worktree paths. Add a real-Git regression test: an empty or nonempty destination nested in a host repo is not reused, and the host's refs, origin, and index stay unchanged. Run the sase verification its `lint_and_test.md` memory prescribes.

task_type_fields.impact: An external repo open can hand agents a path whose Git operations mutate the host bob-cli checkout (local commits and edits); pushes are now refused by the a14bffcdbf push guard.
task_type_fields.repro: git init -q host && mkdir -p host/sase/repos/external/gh/example/child && cd host/sase/repos/external/gh/example/child && git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree (prints true; show-toplevel is the host). _is_valid_git_repo returns True, so sase repo open reuses the path.

issue.creation_reason: The bob-cli-jf.1 guard phase hardened linked and sidecar reuse, but external repo opens still accept an enclosing host checkout, the same failure class that caused the bob-cli-jf incident.

payload.description: Same root-cause class (Git discovery climbing into the host checkout); the jf.1.2 guard fixed linked/sidecar paths and added the is_worktree_root probe to reuse here
